theme: 3 terms on array methods that clean up and reshape data: put items in order, drop nil results and flatten nested arrays

terms.definition: A collection method that returns a new array with the items put in order.

terms.definition: A collection method that changes every item and drops the results that are nil.

terms.example: Use flatMap to join every team's members into one list.

video.title: Sorted, CompactMap & FlatMap in 2 minutes | iOS Daily English Day 26
video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift array methods that clean up data: Sorted, CompactMap & FlatMap, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Sorted - A collection method that returns a new array with the items put in order.
CompactMap - A collection method that changes every item and drops the results that are nil.
FlatMap - A collection method that changes every item into a list and joins all the lists into one flat array.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

dialogue.title: Clean the list, then reshape it

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, my `ages` array has bad text in it. Int fails on `n/a`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use CompactMap with `Int`. It changes every item and drops the nil results.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I tried Sorted first, but the bad text is still there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Sorted only puts items in order. Clean first, then sort.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: OK, CompactMap gives me `valid`. Now Sorted gives me `order`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. Now we have `groups`, an array of arrays. Do you want one list?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, that keeps the inner arrays. Use FlatMap to join them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So FlatMap makes `flat` with just one level?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. FlatMap joins lists, CompactMap drops nil.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. CompactMap to clean, Sorted to order, FlatMap to flatten.
Use sorted to show the highest scores first.
